description:
We are The_Alchemist, a Bangladeshi team, passionate about AI, climate science and agriculture. We are developing VaporPath, a NASA-powered farm resilience simulator.

• Hawarih Hawa: Team leadership, research and NASA data exploration.
• MD Rakib Hasan: Research and strategic planning.
• Md. Naimur Rahman Nahid: Software development and video editing.
• Rafia: Storytelling.
summary:
VaporPath Farm Resilience Simulator is an interactive web platform that turns NASA Earth-observation data into practical farm decisions for South American agriculture. It follows moisture from the Amazon rainforest across the South America region to farmland in Brazil and Argentina. A farmer selects a region, runs a NASA-based farm scan, follows the "Continental Moisture Journey" from the Amazon to the farm, and tests crop and irrigation choices through a what-if simulation that produces a Resilience Score. A GIS dashboard shows the spatial evidence, and an Early Warning Report can be downloaded as a PDF adaptation plan.

It addresses the challenge "Adapting Farms with NASA Data" by using NASA POWER for weather data, NASA Worldview for satellite map layers, and NASA Remote Sensors guidance on monitoring soil moisture, rainfall, and vegetation. Together they turn complex satellite information into clear, actionable steps.

This matters because moisture from the Amazon rainforest supplies rainfall to farmland across South America, and farmers need to recognize water-stress risk before crops are lost. VaporPath is a prototype, and values shown are illustrative where live NASA data is unavailable.
details:
What it does and how it works
VaporPath is a web-based farm resilience simulator. A farmer picks a region (Brazil, Argentina, Bolivia, or Paraguay) and runs a NASA-based farm scan showing root-zone soil moisture, rainfall anomaly, and vegetation stress. The "Continental Moisture Journey" then shows how water moves from the Amazon canopy through the flying rivers and seasonal rainfall to the farm. The farmer chooses crops and irrigation in a what-if simulation, which gives a Resilience Score. A GIS dashboard maps farm sectors and recommends crop rotation, and an Early Warning Report with a soil-moisture trend and forecast can be downloaded as a PDF.

Benefits

  • Farmers can see water-stress risk before crops are damaged.
  • Complex satellite data becomes plain, story-driven guidance.
  • Users can compare crop and irrigation choices, including how much water each saves, before committing.
  • Cooperatives and planners get spatial evidence and a shareable report.

Intended impact
We want to build water resilience and food security across South American farming regions that depend on Amazon moisture. We also want NASA Earth-observation science to be understandable to farmers, students, and the public.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, and software

  • Godot 4 with C# for the interactive browser-based simulations.
  • React, Vite, and Tailwind CSS for the GIS dashboard and NASA observation report.
  • Recharts for the soil-moisture trend charts, and Lucide for the icons.
  • JavaScript, HTML, and CSS for the web layer.
  • NASA POWER API, NASA Worldview, and the NASA Remote Sensors guide as data and reference sources.
  • No special hardware. It runs entirely in a web browser.
  • The full source code and complete list of libraries, including the PDF report export, are in our GitHub repository: https://github.com/hawarihCSE/VaporPath-Agri-Planner

How it is creative
Instead of a data dashboard, we built a farmer-centered game. It starts with a story, gives the farmer decisions to make, and ends with a Resilience Score and a real adaptation plan. It also links a single farm to a continental atmospheric process, the flying rivers.

Factors we considered

  • Accessibility: simple language and visuals for non-technical users.
  • Scientific honesty: VaporPath is a prototype for decision support, not a forecasting replacement. Where live NASA data was unavailable, values are marked as illustrative.
  • No overclaiming: we do not claim that Amazon moisture directly caused conditions at a specific farm. The moisture corridor is an illustrative explanation of a possible regional link.
  • Real farm choices: crop resilience, water use, and irrigation options.
